LD operations

Source: vignettes/ld.Rmd
ld.Rmd

Linkage disequilibrium (LD) is how strongly two variants are inherited together, measured by their correlation r. Every Source carries an LD resource, which answers LD for it: an LD Store on the OpenGWAS API, or your own PLINK Reference. This vignette covers each LD operation: choosing the LD, LD matrices, LD proxies, reflookup and clumping.

Variants are named by ALID, as everywhere in opengwasr (see ALIDs). The sign of r refers to the first allele in each ALID.

Status. Every chunk runs, replayed from responses recorded against the development Data API on 23 November 2026 (ld-resource-api and ld-resource-override replay the same requests as choosing-ld, unassigned-ld and ld-matrices; plink-api and plink-alid-rsids replay requests recorded for Getting started, copied here), except these:

  • stored-clumps: no Store Release has stored Clumps yet; reading them comes in a later step (#39). Its output is illustrative.
  • plink-reference, plink-api, plink-ld-only and plink-alid-rsids: they read the small synthetic PLINK Reference that comes with opengwasr, and need a PLINK binary. They run wherever PLINK 1.9 or 2 is found (plink_ready: genetics.binaRies, or plink or plink2 on the PATH), as in CI; without one, as on CRAN, their code is shown unevaluated.

Developer note: The API responses in this vignette were recorded against the development Data API, directly, with a developer key (see vignettes/recordings.R). Once the OpenGWAS Gateway is live (#18), re-record through it, so the vignettes show the access users will have.

library(opengwasr)
src <- og_api()

LD Stores

An LD Store holds the LD of one reference panel of one ancestry, on GRCh38. og_ld_stores() lists them:

og_ld_stores(src)
##              ld_store ancestry   n      t_far near_bp   far_bp n_variants
## 1 hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10      EUR 665 0.03186544 3000000 10000000    8586889
## 2 hgdp1kgp-v2-AFR-k10      AFR 608 0.03490787 3000000 10000000   14374341
## 3 hgdp1kgp-v2-EAS-k10      EAS 724 0.02922861 3000000 10000000    7837854
## 4 hgdp1kgp-v2-SAS-k10      SAS 672 0.03152799 3000000 10000000    8879035
## 5 hgdp1kgp-v2-AMR-k10      AMR 341 0.06315152 3000000 10000000    7561067
##   default ready
## 1      NA  TRUE
## 2      NA  TRUE
## 3      NA  TRUE
## 4      NA  TRUE
## 5      NA  TRUE
  • n is the number of people whose genotypes the LD Store was built from (HGDP + 1000 Genomes).
  • An LD Store doesn’t hold every pair of variants. Within near_bp (3 Mb) of each other, it holds every pair’s r. From near_bp to far_bp (10 Mb), it holds r only for pairs whose r² reaches its Far Threshold, t_far; for the rest it knows only that r² is below t_far. Beyond far_bp, and across chromosomes, it holds nothing.
  • A variant the LD Store doesn’t cover is absent from it. Every LD operation tells you how many variants were absent.
  • default will mark each ancestry’s default LD Store once the API declares one. Until then it is NA.

Choosing the LD

The Source’s LD resource

A Source says where Associations come from, and which LD resource answers LD for them. The LD is chosen on the Source, and only there: no verb takes an LD argument. An LD resource is one of three kinds, and each can be on the API or on your machine:

LD resource On the API On your machine
LD Store: the precomputed LD of one reference panel og_api(ld_store = "EUR"), an LD Store’s name or an ancestry code. Available now og_local(gwas = ..., ld_store = path). Coming, when opengwasr can read downloaded LD Stores
Genotype Store: genotypes of one reference panel, from which LD is computed when asked og_api(geno_store = ...). Coming, when the API serves Genotype Stores og_local(gwas = ..., geno_store = path). Coming, when opengwasr can read downloaded Genotype Stores
PLINK Reference: your own PLINK binary fileset (.bed, .bim, .fam) None: the API doesn’t read your files og_local(gwas = ..., bfile = prefix), or og_local(bfile = prefix) alone for LD only, and plink = the PLINK 1.9 or 2 binary if opengwasr can’t find it. Available now
None given og_api(): each Analysis’s Assigned Ancestry chooses its LD Store og_local(gwas = ...): anything that needs LD stops and asks you to give an LD resource

LD from a PLINK Reference is computed from its genotypes without adjusting for population structure (principal components), unlike OpenGWAS LD Stores and Genotype Stores, so it may be less accurate. opengwasr warns of this once per PLINK Reference in a session (class opengwasr_plink_unadjusted).

A form that is coming is refused with an error that says so (class opengwasr_ld_resource_unavailable), rather than quietly doing something else. og_api(ld_store = ) takes an LD Store’s name, such as "hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10", or an ancestry code, such as "EUR", for that ancestry’s LD Store (its declared default, if it has several). An exact LD Store name wins; otherwise it is read as an ancestry code. LD Store names and ancestry codes (EUR, AFR, EAS, SAS, AMR) can’t be confused today, and the provenance always records which LD Store was used: a name gives ld_choice = "user" (clump_ld_choice when clumping), an ancestry code "ancestry_default".

Every verb that needs LD uses the Source’s LD resource: og_tophits() when it clumps, og_clump(), og_ld_matrix(), og_ld_proxies() and og_ld_reflookup(). Here the Source’s LD resource is the EUR LD Store, and the top hits are clumped there:

src_eur <- og_api(ld_store = "EUR")
src_eur
## <og_api_source>
## • URL: http://localhost:6433
## • Signed in with: OPENGWAS_DEV_KEY (as opengwasr-dev)
## • Timeout: 3600 s
## • Jobs in flight: at most 4
## • LD resource: LD Store "EUR"
cad_eur <- og_tophits(src_eur, "OGS-00011:GCST003116")
## Warning in og_tophits(src_eur, "OGS-00011:GCST003116"): 234 of the 2,194 top
## hits of OGS-00011:GCST003116 aren't in LD Store hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10, so they
## can't be clumped and were left out.
unique(cad_eur[, c("id", "clump_ld", "clump_ld_choice", "clump_r2", "clump_kb")])
##                     id            clump_ld  clump_ld_choice   clump_r2 clump_kb
## 1 OGS-00011:GCST003116 hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10 ancestry_default 0.03186544    10000

An LD Store named by its name:

cad_eur <- og_tophits(og_api(ld_store = "hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10"), "OGS-00011:GCST003116")
## Warning in og_tophits(og_api(ld_store = "hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10"),
## "OGS-00011:GCST003116"): 234 of the 2,194 top hits of OGS-00011:GCST003116
## aren't in LD Store hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10, so they can't be clumped and were left
## out.
unique(cad_eur$clump_ld_choice)
## [1] "user"

og_ld_resource() returns the LD resource a Source carries (NULL when it carries none). Packages built on opengwasr, such as TwoSampleMR, use it to honour the Source’s LD resource:

og_ld_resource(src_eur)
## [1] "EUR"
og_ld_resource(og_api())
## NULL

A different LD for one call is a different Source

To use other LD for one call, make a Source like the one you have, with other LD. inherit = does it in one line: every argument you give replaces the inherited one, and everything else (the URL, key, timeout and max_in_flight of an API Source; the Store Releases of a Local Source) comes from inherit. Giving any LD argument replaces the inherited LD resource; it is never mixed with it. The one exception is plink alone: og_local(inherit = local, plink = "plink2") keeps the PLINK Reference’s fileset and changes the PLINK that reads it.

src_amr <- og_api(inherit = src_eur, ld_store = "AMR")
basophils <- og_tophits(src_amr, "OGS-00014:GCST90475125")
unique(basophils$clump_ld)
## [1] "hgdp1kgp-v2-AMR-k10"
m <- og_ld_matrix(src_eur, c("16:53772541:A:G", "16:53767042:C:T", "18:60161902:C:T", "2:628504:A:G", "5:75701728:A:AAAAT"))
og_provenance(m)$ld
## [1] "hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10"

src_eur is unchanged, so the LD matrix uses the EUR LD Store. On a Local Source, og_local(inherit = local, bfile = "<prefix>") keeps its Store Releases and gives it a PLINK Reference. inherit must be the same kind of Source: og_api(inherit = local) is refused (class opengwasr_argument).

Associations from one place, LD from another

A Source’s LD resource lives where the Source does: og_api() answers LD from the API’s LD Stores, and og_local() from resources on your machine. To take Associations from one and LD from the other, fetch with one Source and clump with the other, through og_clump() on the data you already have:

Associations LD How
API API og_tophits(og_api(), ids) (matched by Assigned Ancestry), or og_tophits(og_api(ld_store = "EUR"), ids)
Local PLINK og_tophits(og_local(gwas = ..., bfile = ...), ids, r2 = , kb = )
Local API og_clump(og_api(), og_tophits(local, ids, clump = FALSE, limit = 10000))
API PLINK og_clump(og_local(bfile = ...), og_tophits(og_api(), ids, clump = FALSE, limit = 10000), r2 = , kb = )

og_clump() clumps each Analysis’s rows on their own, as og_tophits() does, so every row gives each Analysis its own index variants (Clumping data you already have). In the last two rows, limit = 10000 (the most) fetches every top hit to clump: limit defaults to 1,000, and would cut the top hits off before they are clumped, keeping only the strongest 1,000 of each Analysis. A warning of class opengwasr_truncated says when it does.

The last row uses a Local Source with only a PLINK Reference: an LD-only Local Source. It answers og_clump() and og_ld_matrix() and nothing else (below). The third is in LD from the API’s LD Stores.

The rest of this vignette uses src, made with og_api(), which has no LD resource of its own, so each Analysis’s Assigned Ancestry chooses, and src_eur where one LD Store is named.

Matching by Assigned Ancestry

With no LD resource on the API Source, opengwasr uses the LD Store that matches each Analysis’s Assigned Ancestry, the ancestry opengwasdb inferred from the Analysis’s allele frequencies. Analyses of different ancestries in one call each get their own LD Store. Here, two Analyses’ top hits are clumped (see Clumping):

both <- og_tophits(src, c("OGS-00011:GCST003116", "OGS-00013:GCST90475090"))
unique(both[, c("id", "clump_ld", "clump_ld_choice", "clump_r2", "clump_kb")])
##                        id            clump_ld clump_ld_choice   clump_r2
## 1    OGS-00011:GCST003116 hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10         matched 0.03186544
## 50 OGS-00013:GCST90475090 hgdp1kgp-v2-AFR-k10         matched 0.03490787
##    clump_kb
## 1     10000
## 50    10000

OGS-00013:GCST90475090 (HbA1c, Assigned Ancestry AFR) is clumped against African LD, at that LD Store’s own t_far. A non-European Analysis is never given European LD unless you ask for it. og_clump() matches each Analysis’s own LD Store the same way, from its id column. An LD matrix or LD proxies of a data frame of Associations need one LD Store for all its Analyses, matched from its id column, and og_provenance() records the choice in ld and ld_choice.

If several LD Stores serve one ancestry, opengwasr uses the one the LD Store list declares as that ancestry’s default, and clump_ld_choice (or ld_choice) says "ancestry_default". Today each ancestry has one LD Store. (og_ld_stores()’s default column says which; it is NA until the API declares one, and an ancestry with several LD Stores and no declared default is refused.)

A plain vector of variants has no ancestry to match, so og_ld_matrix() and og_ld_proxies() need the Source’s LD resource when given one.

Unassigned and mixed ancestry

An Analysis whose allele frequencies match no single ancestry confidently is Unassigned (assigned_ancestry is NA in og_analyses()). opengwasr won’t guess an LD Store for it, and never falls back to European LD:

og_tophits(src, "OGS-00014:GCST90475125")
## Error in `og_tophits()`:
## ! Can't choose an LD Store for OGS-00014:GCST90475125: its ancestry is Unassigned.
## ℹ Its allele frequencies match no single ancestry confidently.
## ℹ Give the Source an LD Store, such as `og_api(inherit = src, ld_store = "EUR")`, from: "EUR", "AFR", "EAS", "SAS", "AMR" (see `og_ld_stores()`).
## ℹ Or pass `clump = FALSE` for unclumped top hits.

The error has class opengwasr_ld_unmatched, a kind of opengwasr_refusal, with the LD Stores in e$ld_stores. If you decide AMR LD is right for it (its source describes it as “AMR”), say so, with a Source whose LD resource is the AMR LD Store:

basophils <- og_tophits(og_api(inherit = src, ld_store = "AMR"), "OGS-00014:GCST90475125")
unique(basophils$clump_ld)
## [1] "hgdp1kgp-v2-AMR-k10"

The same refusal applies whenever one LD Store is needed for several Analyses (an LD matrix, or og_clump(by_analysis = FALSE)), and their ancestries differ or one of them is Unassigned. One LD Store is never applied to a different ancestry without your say-so.

LD matrices

og_ld_matrix() returns the signed LD correlation r between every pair of variants, here from src_eur’s EUR LD Store:

m <- og_ld_matrix(
  src_eur,
  c("16:53772541:A:G", "16:53767042:C:T", "18:60161902:C:T", "2:628504:A:G", "5:75701728:A:AAAAT")
)
round(m, 3)
##                    16:53772541:A:G 16:53767042:C:T 18:60161902:C:T 2:628504:A:G
## 16:53772541:A:G              1.000          -0.998              NA           NA
## 16:53767042:C:T             -0.998           1.000              NA           NA
## 18:60161902:C:T                 NA              NA               1           NA
## 2:628504:A:G                    NA              NA              NA            1
## 5:75701728:A:AAAAT              NA              NA              NA           NA
##                    5:75701728:A:AAAAT
## 16:53772541:A:G                    NA
## 16:53767042:C:T                    NA
## 18:60161902:C:T                    NA
## 2:628504:A:G                       NA
## 5:75701728:A:AAAAT                  1
  • The dimension names are ALIDs. The sign of r refers to the first allele in each name. Square it for r².
  • Variants can be rsIDs or ALIDs. rsIDs are translated to ALIDs first, and every ALID of an rsID is included.
  • Absent variants are left out of the matrix, with a warning giving how many; og_provenance(m)$absent lists them.
  • More than 500 variants are split into several Jobs, and the pieces are put back together so that every pair is included.

Given a data frame of Associations, og_ld_matrix() matches the LD Store by the Analyses’ Assigned Ancestry:

cad <- og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST003116")
m <- og_ld_matrix(src, cad)
og_provenance(m)$ld
## [1] "hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10"

Missing pairs, and filling them with 0

A pair the LD Store doesn’t hold is NA, never 0 by default. NA means one of two things:

  • Below the Far Threshold. The two variants are on one chromosome, between near_bp and far_bp apart, and their r² is below t_far. The LD Store knows they are at most weakly linked (for EUR, |r| below about 0.18), but not r itself.
  • Not measured. The two variants are more than far_bp apart, or on different chromosomes. The LD Store holds nothing about them.

Many methods need a number for every pair. fill_below_t_far = TRUE sets the first kind to 0 and leaves the second NA:

v <- c("7:105919152:C:T", "7:105920689:A:G", "7:110998200:C:T", "7:117559403:A:G", "16:53767042:C:T")
round(og_ld_matrix(src_eur, v), 3)
##                 7:105919152:C:T 7:105920689:A:G 7:110998200:C:T 7:117559403:A:G
## 7:105919152:C:T           1.000          -0.182              NA              NA
## 7:105920689:A:G          -0.182           1.000              NA              NA
## 7:110998200:C:T              NA              NA               1              NA
## 7:117559403:A:G              NA              NA              NA               1
## 16:53767042:C:T              NA              NA              NA              NA
##                 16:53767042:C:T
## 7:105919152:C:T              NA
## 7:105920689:A:G              NA
## 7:110998200:C:T              NA
## 7:117559403:A:G              NA
## 16:53767042:C:T               1
round(og_ld_matrix(src_eur, v, fill_below_t_far = TRUE), 3)
##                 7:105919152:C:T 7:105920689:A:G 7:110998200:C:T 7:117559403:A:G
## 7:105919152:C:T           1.000          -0.182               0              NA
## 7:105920689:A:G          -0.182           1.000               0              NA
## 7:110998200:C:T           0.000           0.000               1               0
## 7:117559403:A:G              NA              NA               0               1
## 16:53767042:C:T              NA              NA              NA              NA
##                 16:53767042:C:T
## 7:105919152:C:T              NA
## 7:105920689:A:G              NA
## 7:110998200:C:T              NA
## 7:117559403:A:G              NA
## 16:53767042:C:T               1

7:110998200:C:T is about 5 Mb from the first two variants and 6.6 Mb from 7:117559403:A:G: inside the far window, so those pairs become 0. The first two variants are 11.6 Mb from 7:117559403:A:G, beyond far_bp, so those pairs stay NA, as do all pairs with the chromosome 16 variant.

The option is off by default because 0 claims more than the LD Store knows: only that r² is below t_far. Within near_bp nothing is missing, so it changes nothing there. A matrix from a PLINK Reference has every pair, so the option doesn’t apply.

LD proxies

og_ld_proxies() finds the variants in LD with each variant you give: every variant within kb kilobases whose r² with it is at least r2 (defaults 0.8 and 10,000 kb). Strongest first:

px <- og_ld_proxies(src_eur, "16:53767042:C:T")
nrow(px)
## [1] 98
head(px, 5)
##              alid      proxy_alid          r        r2 distance
## 1 16:53767042:C:T 16:53768582:C:T -1.0000000 1.0000000     1540
## 2 16:53767042:C:T 16:53769311:A:G  1.0000000 1.0000000     2269
## 3 16:53767042:C:T 16:53769662:A:T  1.0000000 1.0000000     2620
## 4 16:53767042:C:T 16:53775211:C:T -1.0000000 1.0000000     8169
## 5 16:53767042:C:T 16:53772541:A:G -0.9980431 0.9960899     5499
  • r is signed for the first alleles of alid and proxy_alid; distance is in base pairs.
  • Variants can be rsIDs or ALIDs, or a data frame of Associations, whose Analyses’ Assigned Ancestry then chooses the LD Store.
  • Absent variants have no LD proxies, and a warning (class opengwasr_ld_absent_variants) gives how many.
  • r2 and kb follow the same rule as clumping: below t_far, kb can be at most 3,000 (Your own r² and window). Otherwise the API refuses (opengwasr_ld_refusal, with reason, t_far, near_bp and far_bp).

This is an LD lookup, for questions about LD itself: which variants tag a signal, or which variants to look for in data from outside OpenGWAS. It is not the LD-proxy substitution ieugwasr made when an outcome lacked a variant. opengwasr never swaps another variant’s Association in for a missing one; Reference-Completed Store Releases hold Imputed Associations instead (see Imputed Associations).

Is a variant in the LD Store?

og_ld_reflookup() says whether the LD Store holds each variant, so you can check instruments before clumping or building an LD matrix. It returns one row per variant asked, with alid, rsid (when known) and present:

og_ld_reflookup(src_eur, c("16:53767042:C:T", "rs1421085", "16:53767042:A:C"))
##              alid      rsid present
## 1 16:53767042:C:T      <NA>    TRUE
## 2 16:53767042:C:T rs1421085    TRUE
## 3 16:53767042:A:G rs1421085   FALSE
## 4 16:53767042:A:C      <NA>   FALSE
  • An rsID stands for every ALID it names, one row each: rs1421085 names two ALIDs here, and the LD Store holds one of them. An rsID no GWAS Store holds has one row with alid NA and present FALSE.
  • A variant the LD Store doesn’t hold is a row, not a warning; og_provenance() lists them as absent.
  • The LD Store is chosen as for the other LD functions, and only an LD Store can answer: a Local Source, whose LD is a PLINK Reference, is refused.

Clumping

Clumping keeps one variant per independent signal.

Top hits are clumped by default

og_tophits() clumps unless you pass clump = FALSE:

cad <- og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST003116")
## Warning in og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST003116"): 234 of the 2,194 top hits
## of OGS-00011:GCST003116 aren't in LD Store hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10, so they can't
## be clumped and were left out.
nrow(cad)
## [1] 49
head(cad[, c("rsid", "alid", "beta", "pval", "clump_size")], 5)
##          rsid            alid        beta         pval clump_size
## 1   rs2891168  9:22098620:A:G -0.19335911 2.296241e-98        193
## 2  rs55730499 6:160584578:C:T -0.31671619 5.392728e-39         94
## 3   rs7528419 1:109274570:A:G  0.11453085 1.968746e-23          9
## 4   rs4711863  6:12915185:C:G -0.09856474 1.613590e-21         96
## 5 rs115654617 2:203029276:A:C  0.13790739 3.119371e-18        316

The 2,194 top hits at p ≤ 5e-8 reduce to 49 index variants. clump_size counts the top hits each index variant stands for, itself included.

  • Variants are ranked by |z|. Starting from the strongest, each index variant absorbs every weaker top hit within kb kilobases whose r² with it is above r2 (the rule plink --clump uses).
  • Every top hit at the threshold is clumped, and limit (default 1,000) then caps the index variants returned.
  • Absent top hits can’t be clumped. They are left out, with a warning giving how many, and the count is kept in the provenance.

Stored Clumps, and clumping on the fly

clump = TRUE is the default, and clump = FALSE gives every top hit, unclumped. A set of Clumps is always made with one configuration: an LD resource, r2 and kb.

  • Stored Clumps. Store Releases will carry Clumps made when each release was built: its 5e-8 top hits, clumped with each ancestry’s default LD resource and its r2 and kb. The default call, og_tophits(src, ids), will read them, so it needs no LD resource at all, on either Source. They are used only when your request matches that configuration exactly, never when it is merely close. Today’s Store Releases don’t have stored Clumps yet.
  • Clumping on the fly. Until a Store Release has them, clump = TRUE clumps on the fly, with the Source’s LD resource. Any other threshold, r2, kb or LD resource is always clumped on the fly, with the Source’s LD resource.
  • Provenance says which. og_provenance(x)$clump records the LD resource, r2 and kb used, and in clumps whether the Clumps were "stored" or "computed".

Once a Store Release has stored Clumps, the default call reads them:

cad <- og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST003116")
og_provenance(cad)$clump[, c("id", "ld", "r2", "kb", "leads", "clumps")]
# illustrative
                    id                  ld         r2    kb leads clumps
1 OGS-00011:GCST003116 hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10 0.03186544 10000    49 stored

Default thresholds come from the LD Store

You don’t need to choose r2 and kb. By default, opengwasr clumps within the LD Store’s far window (10,000 kb), at its Far Threshold t_far (about 0.03). That is always a question the LD Store can answer exactly.

ieugwasr’s default, r² 0.001 within 10,000 kb, is not. Beyond 3,000 kb an LD Store keeps only pairs with r² ≥ t_far, so it can’t tell an r² of 0.001 from one of 0.02 there. If you ask for it, opengwasr refuses.

Your own r² and window, and reading a refusal

Pass r2 and kb to clump with your own thresholds. If the LD Store can answer them exactly, it does. If not, the API refuses and says why, and opengwasr passes its message on. It never clumps at something close to what you asked.

og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST003116", r2 = 0.001, kb = 10000)
## Error in `og_tophits()`:
## ! r2=0.001 is below t_far=0.03186544342507645: beyond 3,000,000 bp the store holds only the Bound r² < t_far for unstored pairs, which does not decide r̂² ≥ r2

The message is the API’s. The error has class opengwasr_ld_refusal, a kind of opengwasr_refusal. It carries the API’s reason and the LD Store’s limits as fields, so a script can decide what to do: here, any r2 is answered within near_bp, 3,000 kb, and an r2 of at least t_far within far_bp, 10,000 kb. Catch opengwasr_ld_refusal itself to read those fields; the parent class opengwasr_refusal also covers refusals that don’t have them:

cad_strict <- tryCatch(
  og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST003116", r2 = 0.001, kb = 10000),
  opengwasr_ld_refusal = function(e) {
    message("Refused (", e$reason, "); clumping within ", e$near_bp / 1000, " kb instead.")
    og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST003116", r2 = 0.001, kb = e$near_bp / 1000)
  }
)
## Refused (threshold_below_t_far); clumping within 3000 kb instead.

Fields, as the API sends them: e$reason (here "threshold_below_t_far"), e$store (the LD Store), e$ancestry, e$t_far, e$near_bp and e$far_bp. og_ld_proxies() refuses in the same way.

Clumping data you already have

og_clump() clumps a data frame of Associations you already have, such as top hits fetched unclumped from another Source. It needs alid and z, and an id column saying which Analysis each row is from. It takes r2 and kb exactly as og_tophits() does, and uses the Source’s LD resource.

  • Each Analysis is clumped on its own (by_analysis = TRUE, the default), as og_tophits() does, so og_clump(src, og_tophits(src, ids, clump = FALSE, limit = 10000)) gives each Analysis the same index variants as og_tophits(src, ids).
  • Each Analysis gets its own LD Store: with no LD resource on the API Source, the one matching its Assigned Ancestry, as in Matching by Assigned Ancestry, so Analyses of different ancestries can be clumped in one call.
  • The rows come back in their order in data: the rows of each Analysis’s index variants, with the clumping columns.
  • A data frame with no id column is one set. It has no Assigned Ancestry to match, so the Source needs an LD resource, such as og_clump(src_eur, data).

To clump several Analyses together, as one set whose index variants compete, such as the instruments of a multivariable MR, pass by_analysis = FALSE: a variant listed several times is then ranked by its largest |z|, every Association of a kept variant is returned, and with no LD resource on the API Source every Analysis must share one Assigned Ancestry (else opengwasr_ld_unmatched, as above). Here the 100 strongest index variants of BMI and of LDL cholesterol are clumped together:

bmi <- og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST90029007", limit = 100)
ldl <- og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST90002412", limit = 100)
joint <- og_clump(src, rbind(bmi, ldl), by_analysis = FALSE)
table(joint$id)
## 
## OGS-00011:GCST90002412 OGS-00011:GCST90029007 
##                    100                     97

Clumping provenance

Every clumped data frame records how it was clumped, in columns that survive subsetting, merging and binding:

Column Meaning
clump_ld The LD Store’s name, or the PLINK Reference’s path
clump_ld_choice How it was chosen: "matched" (the one LD Store for the Analysis’s Assigned Ancestry), "ancestry_default" (an ancestry’s default LD Store: the Source’s ld_store is an ancestry code, or the Assigned Ancestry has several LD Stores) or "user" (the Source names an LD Store, or carries a PLINK Reference)
clump_r2, clump_kb The r² and window applied, whether defaults or yours
clump_size How many top hits the index variant stands for

og_provenance() (defined in Getting started) adds the counts behind them. Unlike the columns, it doesn’t survive rbind():

og_provenance(cad)
## ── opengwasr provenance ─────────────────
## • Query: og_tophits(threshold = 5e-08, limit = 1000, observed_only = FALSE, clump = TRUE, original_units = FALSE)
## • Store Releases: OGS-00011/OGS-00011-completed
## • LD Store: ancestry (); 0 variant(s) absent
## • Clumped: OGS-00011:GCST003116 in hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10 (matched), r² 0.0319 within 10,000 kb; 2,194 top hits, 234 not in the LD Store, 49 index variants, computed
## • Jobs: 86d6e51a
## • Rows: 49 returned of 49 matching
## • Retrieved: 2026-11-26 10:17:34 UTC
og_provenance(cad)$clump
##                     id                  ld ld_choice         r2    kb hits
## 1 OGS-00011:GCST003116 hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10   matched 0.03186544 10000 2194
##   absent leads   clumps
## 1    234    49 computed

hits counts the top hits at the threshold, absent those the LD Store doesn’t hold, and leads the index variants. clumps says whether the Clumps were "computed" on the fly, as they all are today, or read "stored" with the Store Release (Stored Clumps). Two clumpings that differ can be explained from these alone.

Using a PLINK Reference

A PLINK Reference is a PLINK binary genotype fileset (.bed, .bim, .fam) on your own machine, such as the 1000 Genomes files ieugwasr users already have. It is the LD resource of a Local Source, given as bfile, and PLINK 1.9 or PLINK 2 reads it on your machine, as ieugwasr’s local functions did:

  • og_local(gwas = ..., bfile = prefix): Associations from your Store Releases, LD from your PLINK Reference (Clumping and LD on a Local Source).
  • og_local(bfile = prefix): an LD-only Local Source, with no Store Releases. It answers og_clump() and og_ld_matrix() for data you already have, such as top hits from the API Source: the last row of the table above.

For your own, such as og_local(bfile = "~/ld/1kg/EUR"), the calls are og_clump(ld_src, og_tophits(src, ids, clump = FALSE, limit = 10000), r2 = 0.001, kb = 10000) and og_ld_matrix(ld_src, rsids). Here, the small synthetic PLINK Reference that comes with opengwasr, 300 made-up people, whose rsIDs include a few of the CAD and BMI index variants from above, clumps those of each Analysis on their own, and reads an LD matrix of rsIDs. It holds only a few of these real variants, so most are left out, as the message says; your own PLINK Reference holds far more:

ld_src <- og_local(bfile = file.path(system.file("plink", package = "opengwasr"), "ref"))
ld_src
## <og_local_source>
## • Store Releases: none (LD only)
## • LD resource: PLINK Reference /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/opengwasr/plink/ref
##   PLINK 1.90b6.21: /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/genetics.binaRies/bin/plink
og_ld_resource(ld_src)$plink_version   # the PLINK that was found, 1.9 or 2
## [1] "1.90b6.21"
clumped_local <- og_clump(ld_src, rbind(cad, bmi), r2 = 0.001, kb = 10000)
## ℹ 7 of 149 variants matched the PLINK Reference by rsID; 142 not in it
## were left out.
## Warning in og_clump(ld_src, rbind(cad, bmi), r2 = 0.001, kb = 10000): LD from a PLINK Reference is computed from its genotypes without adjusting for population structure (principal components), unlike OpenGWAS LD Stores and Genotype Stores, so it may be less accurate.
## ℹ PLINK Reference: /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/opengwasr/plink/ref.
## This warning is displayed once per session.
clumped_local[, c("id", "rsid", "alid", "z", "clump_r2", "clump_kb", "clump_size")]
##                       id       rsid            alid          z clump_r2
## 1   OGS-00011:GCST003116  rs2891168  9:22098620:A:G -21.049805    0.001
## 2   OGS-00011:GCST003116 rs55730499 6:160584578:C:T -13.062500    0.001
## 3   OGS-00011:GCST003116  rs7528419 1:109274570:A:G   9.974609    0.001
## 4   OGS-00011:GCST003116  rs4711863  6:12915185:C:G  -9.527344    0.001
## 5 OGS-00011:GCST90029007 rs56094641 16:53772541:A:G -38.534206    0.001
## 6 OGS-00011:GCST90029007  rs6567160 18:60161902:C:T  23.840820    0.001
## 7 OGS-00011:GCST90029007   rs539515 1:177919890:A:C -19.618164    0.001
##   clump_kb clump_size
## 1    10000          1
## 2    10000          1
## 3    10000          1
## 4    10000          1
## 5    10000          1
## 6    10000          1
## 7    10000          1
m_local <- og_ld_matrix(ld_src, c("rs4977574", "rs2891168", "rs1333049", "rs1421085"))
round(m_local, 3)
##               rs4977574_G_A rs2891168_G_A rs1333049_C_G rs1421085_C_T
## rs4977574_G_A         1.000         0.701         0.085        -0.011
## rs2891168_G_A         0.701         1.000         0.024         0.045
## rs1333049_C_G         0.085         0.024         1.000         0.033
## rs1421085_C_T        -0.011         0.045         0.033         1.000
  • Variants are matched by rsID, because PLINK References are usually on GRCh37 while ALIDs are on GRCh38. Variants without an rsID match are left out, and the message says how many. An LD matrix from a PLINK Reference is named <rsid>_<allele>_<allele> with the PLINK Reference’s alleles, as ieugwasr named it, and the sign of r again refers to the first allele in each name.
  • Its LD isn’t adjusted for principal components. LD from a PLINK Reference is computed from its genotypes without adjusting for population structure (principal components), unlike OpenGWAS LD Stores and Genotype Stores, so it may be less accurate. opengwasr warns of this once per PLINK Reference in a session (class opengwasr_plink_unadjusted). The chunk above shows the warning.
  • r2 and kb are required. A PLINK Reference has no recorded defaults, so opengwasr won’t choose for you. Without them, og_tophits() and og_clump() stop and ask for both.
  • Each Analysis is clumped on its own, one PLINK run per Analysis, as og_tophits() does on a Local Source with a PLINK Reference, so top hits from the API get the index variants og_tophits() would give with this PLINK Reference.
  • PLINK itself is PLINK 1.9, or PLINK 2 from build 2.0.0-a.6.0 (November 2024) on, the first with every option opengwasr uses. og_local(bfile = , plink = ) takes its path, or a command on your PATH such as plink = "plink2"; as in a shell, a name without a / is a command. Without plink, opengwasr looks in the genetics.binaRies package if it is installed, then for plink, then plink2, on your PATH, and takes the first that is a supported PLINK. Another program called plink, such as PuTTY’s, or an older PLINK, is skipped. If none is supported, the error (class opengwasr_plink_not_found) lists what it skipped, in skipped, and says how to install PLINK.
  • Its version is read once, when the Source is made, and kept on its PLINK Reference (og_ld_resource(ld_src)$plink_version) and in provenance (og_provenance(x)$plink_version, beside plink_bin). A PLINK you name that isn’t supported, such as 1.07, is refused (class opengwasr_plink_unsupported, with the version found and the versions supported). If a supported plink or plink2 is on your PATH, the error suggests it.
  • PLINK 1.9 and PLINK 2 give the same answer. opengwasr asks each for the same thing in its own words: an LD matrix of r with the reference’s allele order kept (--r square --keep-allele-order in 1.9, --r-unphased square ref-based in 2), and clumping with --clump, read from .clumped or .clumps. On the PLINK Reference that comes with opengwasr, both give the same clumps, and r equal to within 1e-6.
  • og_ld_proxies() and og_ld_reflookup() read LD Stores only, so a Local Source refuses them.
  • Provenance works as before: clump_ld is the PLINK Reference’s path, and clump_ld_choice is "user".

Top hits from the API, clumped with PLINK

The last row of the table, end to end: BMI’s top hits from the API Source, unclumped, then clumped with the PLINK Reference, each Analysis on its own. Here limit is left at its default, so the warning says the API’s top hits were cut off at 1,000 before clumping; with your own, pass limit = 10000 to clump them all:

bmi_hits <- og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST90029007", clump = FALSE)
## Warning in og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST90029007", clump = FALSE): OGS-00011:GCST90029007 has more than 1,000 top hits at p <= 5e-08; only the strongest 1,000 were returned.
## ℹ Raise `limit` (at most 10,000) for more.
bmi_local <- og_clump(ld_src, bmi_hits, r2 = 0.001, kb = 10000)
## ℹ 6 of 1,000 variants matched the PLINK Reference by rsID; 994 not in
## it were left out.
bmi_local[, c("id", "rsid", "alid", "z", "clump_size")]
##                       id       rsid            alid         z clump_size
## 1 OGS-00011:GCST90029007 rs56094641 16:53772541:A:G -38.53421          1
## 2 OGS-00011:GCST90029007  rs1421085 16:53767042:C:T  38.52622          3
## 3 OGS-00011:GCST90029007  rs6567160 18:60161902:C:T  23.84082          1
## 4 OGS-00011:GCST90029007   rs539515 1:177919890:A:C -19.61816          1
og_provenance(bmi_local)$clump[, c("ld_choice", "r2", "kb", "hits", "absent", "leads", "clumps")]
##   ld_choice    r2    kb hits absent leads   clumps
## 1      user 0.001 10000 1000    994     4 computed

An LD-only Local Source

An LD-only Local Source has no Store Releases, so it has nothing to look an ALID’s rsID up in, and never calls the API. Give it variants it can match by rsID: a data frame with an rsid column, such as any top hits or Associations, or rsIDs. ALIDs alone are refused (class opengwasr_gwas_store_required, with the ALIDs in alids), and the error names the ways round, in forms: give the Source the Store Releases that hold them, og_local(gwas = ..., bfile = ...) ("gwas"); pass a data frame with an rsid column ("rsid_column"); or look their rsIDs up on the API first ("api_rsids"). Every verb that reads Associations refuses it with the same class:

og_ld_matrix(ld_src, c("9:22125504:C:G", "9:22098575:A:G"))
## Error in `og_ld_matrix()`:
## ! This Local Source holds no Store Releases to look up the rsIDs of 2 ALIDs (9:22125504:C:G, 9:22098575:A:G), which its PLINK Reference matches by rsID.
## ℹ Give it the Store Releases too: `og_local(gwas = , bfile = )`, or `og_local(inherit = src, gwas = )`.
## ℹ Or pass a data frame with an `rsid` column, such as top hits or Associations, or rsIDs.
## ℹ Or look the rsIDs up on the API first: `og_variants_chrpos(og_api(), positions)` gives each ALID's `rsid`, for `positions` its "chromosome:position".
og_tophits(ld_src, "OGS-00011:GCST003116")
## Error in `og_tophits()`:
## ! This Local Source holds no Store Releases: it was made with only a PLINK Reference (`og_local(bfile = )`), for LD.
## ℹ Give it the Store Releases too: `og_local(gwas = , bfile = )`, or `og_local(inherit = src, gwas = )`.

To look the rsIDs up on the API, ask og_variants_chrpos() for the ALIDs’ positions, and take the rsid of each ALID; then read the LD matrix of those rsIDs from the PLINK Reference:

alids <- c("16:53767042:C:T")
positions <- sub(":[^:]+:[^:]+$", "", alids)   # chromosome:position
found <- og_variants_chrpos(src, positions, releases = "OGS-00011")
rs <- found$rsid[match(alids, found$alid)]
rs
## [1] "rs1421085"
og_ld_matrix(ld_src, c(rs, "rs9939609"))
##               rs1421085_C_T rs9939609_A_T
## rs1421085_C_T      1.000000      0.519285
## rs9939609_A_T      0.519285      1.000000
